what: The command post's on-device read of a sighting note (readSightingText with sightingTextGenerator, ONLY_ON_DEVICE, the same path as CommandPost's readNote), measured on a local page with the same code path (local page, same code path). Five made-up drill notes read once each, in a row, in a newly opened page.
browser: Stephen's Google Chrome stable on this Mac (macOS, Apple M5 Pro); the built-in model reported available for text; the Chrome and model versions were not recorded
page: web/harness/note-measure.html (dev server http://127.0.0.1:5175), bare Firebase app with no App Check and no sign-in, at the commit that adds the page
note: Read 1 is the first in the newly opened page. About 20 minutes earlier the same browser had read photos on its model (2026-11-21-photo-read-chrome.json), so this is one first-read sample, not a worst case. The command post gave a note read 30,000 ms (NOTE_READ_TIMEOUT_MS).

runs.note: Training drill. Caller saw an older man in a blue coat and grey trousers walking north on the path, carrying a brown bag.
Training drill. A woman in a red jacket and black pants, white sneakers, heading east toward the road.
Training drill. Man in a green sweater and brown slacks going downstream along the creek, holding a cane.
Training drill. Someone in a yellow raincoat and blue jeans was seen walking south past the gate.
Training drill. An older woman in a purple cardigan and tan skirt, moving west across the field with a small dog.

findings: The first read took 27,900 ms, within 7% of the command post's 30,000 ms limit; the next four took 2.3 to 2.9 s. A slower laptop's first note read would be refused.
14 of 15 stated fields right. The miss: "grey trousers" came back unknown; the colour list spells it gray.
All five reads ran on device as the SDK reported, and the page made no request to a Google or Firebase host.
